LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyWards: A youth fostered for a year either way, and hostages given for a truce's or a pact's terms.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyWards_Tip: A people at peace whose head thinks 30 or more of the colony may offer a youth of their town (a child where the game has children, else 14 to 19) to live at the colony for a year and learn a skill it is known for, at most once a year; or the colony asks by letter. The ward lives as the game's lodger, on the colonist bar and working with the colony, and their guardian (a colonist with 10 or more in the skill) teaches them an hour a day when both are free and together; a child with Biotech learns at the game's own lessons instead. At the year's end their family come to the gate for them, and how they were kept (taught, fed, unhurt, content) moves their people: a year kept well leaves a debt of honor, and the grown ward still thinks well of the colony. The colony may offer one of its own youths to live with another people for a year; they write home every ten days and come back with what that people are good at and a friend there (with the Empire, a page in a titled household, for regard only). Hostages, adults only, may be given for a truce or a defense pact either way: theirs lives at the colony for the term, the colony's at their town. Their side breaking the terms leaves theirs the colony's to decide about; the colony breaking them leaves its own held by their people, in the game's own captivity. Off: nothing new is agreed, and those under way run their term.
